title: What Stays? Angular Momentum Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A ball whirled on a string. A planet circling the Sun. A stone in a sling. When Diya whirls a ball over her head, its speed stays the same, but its direction, and so its momentum, changes every moment. Does anything about its motion stay the same? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn the angular momentum of a particle.

On a live motion notebook a ball on a string goes around Diya's hand while the readout tracks r, p and L, and a graph shows the x part of momentum swinging while L stays flat. A longer string gives more angular momentum. Then a surprise: a ball rolling in a straight line past Diya also has angular momentum, and a slow-mo replay shows why: the perpendicular distance from her to its line never changes. We build L = r cross p step by step (L = r p sin theta, L = r perpendicular times p, L = m v r = m r squared omega, units and the right hand rule), compare a circle with a straight line, and work out L for a particle in vector form. Then the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question on a projectile, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
